# HMPFL WEEK 3: LOCKDOWN RECAP

The cell doors slammed shut on another wild week in His Majesty's Prison Fantasy League, and somebody needs to check on the warden because a few of these scorelines are criminal.

## The Great Escape: DUIiiiiiiii Torches the Yard

Let's start with the headline: **DUIiiiiiiii dont know jim** didn't just beat Rice, Rice Baby ✨, he staged a full-blown prison break, dropping a jaw-dropping **367.45 points** in a **113.4-point blowout**. That's not a win, that's a warden's confession that the whole facility is being run by inmates now. Jahmyr Gibbs (72.8) and Drake London (47.3) both went full riot mode, and the Minnesota defense chipped in a stunning 49.45 points, because apparently everyone on this roster got the memo to show up big. Rice, Rice Baby's 254.05 points would've won most other matchups this week — instead it just got buried under an avalanche.

## Squeaker of the Week

While DUIiiiiiiii was out here setting the yard on fire, **Ruggs, Drugs and TDs** and **The Massage Boys** were fighting it out in the closest scrap of the week. The Massage Boys survived, 182.8–164.2, thanks in large part to Sam Darnold (62.4) and Jaxon Smith-Njigba (56.0) doing double duty in what might be the quietest 18.6-point margin of the season — still a W, still counts on the books.

## Cellblock Standouts

Bijan Robinson put on a clinic for **The Adrian BeatHisSons**, exploding for 73.1 points — the single best individual outing of the week — and pairing with Matthew Stafford's 47.6 to help fend off a scrappy **Glove Don't Fit, Blitz** squad, 249.7–227.7, in a game that had shootout energy from kickoff to final whistle.

Meanwhile, **Steve Ruggs** rode Brock Purdy's 70-point gem (plus Joe Burrow chipping in 46.3 — yes, two elite QBs on one roster, that should be illegal) to a 235.85–206.05 win over The ConVicks, whose Tyler Shough tried valiantly with 44.2 points but couldn't spring the upset.

## Other Notes From the Block

**Smack My Diggs Up** handled business against Josh Allen's Prison Cell, 147.9–127.7, while **Hernandez Hitmen** put together a workmanlike 201.45–142 win over OJ's Denver Bronco. No fireworks, just quiet time served.

Book 'em, Week 3. Week 4's already looking like it needs its own warden.
